topStory.headline: Tusculum University Hosts Public A.I. Summit for Broader Community
topStory.summary:
Tusculum University, a private institution with fewer than 3,000 students in rural Tennessee, is hosting a public summit on artificial intelligence, according to WJHL. The event aims to educate the broader community about A.I.'s implications and applications, marking a departure from typical academic conference formats that target only higher education professionals.

The summit reflects a model where regional universities serve as bridges between emerging technology and everyday communities. While flagship universities and R1 institutions pursue A.I. research labs and major partnerships, smaller regional institutions like Tusculum are positioning themselves as community educators.

As A.I. tools become ubiquitous in workplaces from healthcare to manufacturing, rural and smaller communities often lack access to quality information about these technologies. Universities filling this gap can provide evidence-based, accessible education that helps community members make informed decisions about A.I. in their personal and professional lives.

stories.headline: University of Michigan Faculty Split on A.I. Integration
stories.summary: University of Michigan's decentralized A.I. policy creates campus-wide inconsistency, with some departments embracing A.I. while others resist, according to MLive. Faculty report 90% of students already use generative A.I., highlighting a gap between institutional hesitation and student adoption reality.

stories.headline: St. Bonaventure to Provide Campus-Wide ChatGPT Access
stories.summary: St. Bonaventure University in New York will offer ChatGPT Edu licenses to all undergraduates and faculty starting fall 2026, according to The Wellsville Sun. The move follows a 300-person pilot program and represents an institutional commitment to A.I. integration with enterprise-grade security.

stories.headline: UMass Boston Researchers Warn of 'Learning Erosion' From A.I.
stories.summary: UMass Boston researchers argue that A.I.'s greatest threat to higher education is not cheating but the hollowing out of learning ecosystems, according to Cobb Courier. As machines handle more cognitive work, universities risk losing the "productive struggle" that builds genuine expertise and critical thinking skills.

stories.headline: Northeastern Creates A.I. Focus Groups for Strategic Planning
stories.summary: Faculty senate discussions at Northeastern University reveal 90% of students use generative A.I., prompting university-wide planning initiatives, according to The Huntington News. Six focus groups will include faculty, students, and external partners to develop comprehensive A.I. integration strategies.

stories.headline: Colorado Boulder Schedules A.I. Leadership Discussion
stories.summary: Senior Vice Chancellor Janel Forde will lead a March 12 fireside chat on A.I. and higher education at the University of Colorado Boulder, according to CU Boulder Today. The event reflects growing administrative focus on A.I. strategy at the institutional leadership level.
